summary: Preserve reader-visible legacy status transitions during checkpoint trimming

replay.detail: No new startup replay trigger or projection algorithm is introduced. Checkpoint proofs retain their existing scratch-copy before/after replay; source diagnostics are collected during those same reads. A checkpoint rules bump alone does not establish startup replay or health recovery.

schema.detail: No database table, index, trigger, schema-version or migration change.

rules.detail: Rules 13 makes status-history retention select the same non-heartbeat sources as the reader before reducing transitions. Coordinated fleet upgrades are required: participants with different rules digests cannot agree on new seals. Verification refuses stale seal rules without consuming first verification. The normal lifecycle replaces terms for the newest due cut only; older unverified checkpoints need explicit supported verification or clean supersession.

compatibility.detail: No public client, replicated claim, pairing or provider-admission wire change. Diagnostic-only runtime source metadata does not enter reader answers or checkpoint certificates. Mixed checkpoint-rule behavior is classified under rules.

downtime.detail: Restart-to-API and restart-to-health times for this source have not been measured. Deploy through the normal rolling fleet lifecycle and verify health separately from API availability; local scratch-proof passes do not qualify production downtime.

manual.detail: Existing stores mixing unstamped legacy observations and explicitly suppressed heartbeats are affected. Upgrade all checkpoint participants to matching rules, preserve existing participant and first-verification fences, and verify the affected old cuts or record clean supersession through the supported Operations lifecycle. A quiet newest-cut retry does not establish acceptance of an older cut. See docs/st3/checkpoints.md and docs/st3/replication.md. Any remaining normal proof mismatch logs bounded source metadata without transcripts or an extra proof loop.

recovery.detail: Roll forward to matching rules 13 builds. Swapping back to rules 12 restores the reader/planner defect and mismatched rule digests stall new agreement; a binary reinstall does not undo completed trims. This change adds no migration, weakens no preservation proof, and does not authorize bypassing participant or verification fences.
